title: 1952 AHSME Problem 37
statement: Two equal parallel chords are drawn \(8\) inches apart in a circle of radius \(8\) inches. The area of that part of the circle that lies between the chords is:

solutions.text:
The equal chords are symmetrically \(4\) inches from the center. For either chord, the half-angle at the center satisfies \(\cos\theta=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2},\) so \(\theta=60^\circ.\) Each outer segment is a \(120^\circ\) sector minus the isosceles triangle: \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{120}{360}\pi(8)^2 -\frac12(8)^2\sin120^\circ\\ &\qquad=\frac{64\pi}{3}-16\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \] The area between the chords is therefore \[ \begin{aligned} &64\pi-2\left(\frac{64\pi}{3}-16\sqrt3\right)\\ &\qquad=\frac{64\pi}{3}+32\sqrt3\\ &\qquad=21\frac13\pi+32\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Equal parallel chords lie the same distance from the center, so each is \(4\) inches from it
Subtract the two congruent outer circular segments from the whole circle
